primitives.name: Data Replication Method
primitives.verbatim_quote: Replicate each training point twice into R^{d+1}: [x; h] and [x; 0] (h = const).

primitives.verbatim_quote: Train one binary classifier on the 2l replicated points; its intersection with each replica subspace yields two non-intersecting boundaries.

reasoning_traces.think:
The data replication method transforms a ternary classification task into a binary one by duplicating each sample in an extended feature space. Each point becomes two instances: one with a fixed offset h in the extra dimension, and another with zero in that dimension. Training a single binary classifier on these replicated points results in two distinct decision boundaries—one per replica—defining a reject region between them. This construction avoids intersecting boundaries typical in multi-class approaches and sidesteps complex optimization of embedded SVMs. The method is mathematically equivalent to defining a ternary classifier with ordered outputs C1 < C_reject < C2, where the reject region arises naturally from the geometric separation in the extended space. It supports any binary classifier type (e.g., SVMs, neural networks) and enables principled, trainable abstention without post-processing thresholds.
